meaning: The number 232 is linked to the numerical value (gematria) of the phrase "Yehi or" (יהי אור), which means "Let there be light" from Genesis 1:3.
description: In Jewish gematria tradition, the Hebrew letters in "Yehi or" (יהי אור) have a combined numerical value of 232: יהי (Yod + He + Yod = 10+5+10 = 25) and אור (Alef + Vav + Resh = 1+6+200 = 207), totaling 232. This connects the number directly to God's first command in creation, symbolizing divine light, revelation, and the beginning of God's creative work. Thus, the number 232 carries deep theological significance as an expression of God's will to bring light into darkness—the very foundation of all creation.

footnotes.text: In Kabbalistic tradition, 232 is also linked to God's four-letter name (YHVH). The sum of the four known milui expansions of YHVH – Ab (72), Sag (63), Mah (45) and Ban (52) – totals 232. This reinforces the number's mystical meaning as an expression of the fullness of the divine name.
In 1 Kings 20:15, the number 232 appears in a historical context: King Ahab mustered 232 young men who served the provincial governors before going into battle against the Aramean king Ben-Hadad.
